_comment: Example vars.json shape for populate_template.py. The example below illustrates a complete report for Pacific Coast Plumbing (mock_response.json). Replace per-client. Section 08 now uses a 3-batch structure; the legacy flat 'employees' array still works (it auto-wraps as Batch 01).
cover_subtitle: Six tools, phased over twelve weeks, get you your evenings back — and put the books, the quotes, and the receivables on a tight loop without you typing a single line.
exec_summary_lede: You told us you want to grow to fifteen staff without you being the bottleneck on every job. You also told us, plainly, that you're doing books at the kitchen table on Sunday night. This report is about closing the gap between those two sentences.
exec_summary_para_2: Six tools, phased over twelve weeks, do most of the work. We've leaned toward provider-vetted defaults and integrations that don't need glue layers — your tech appetite is medium and we respect that.
exec_summary_para_3: The numbers on the next page are conservative ranges based on Fair Work AU 2026 rates. The point is not that you'll hit every dollar, every month — it's that the headroom is real, and the path to capturing it is clear.
_priority_actions_note: Five priority actions for section 02. If omitted, the template derives them from the top 5 recs[]. Each item: action (title with tool name), fix (one-line pain description), outcome (the win after doing it).

priority_actions.action: Move to ServiceM8 for job and dispatch management
priority_actions.fix: Stop losing job sheets to the back of the ute
priority_actions.outcome: Every job tracked from quote to invoice in one place

priority_actions.fix: End Sunday-night re-typing at the kitchen table

priority_actions.action: Move to professional email on Google Workspace
priority_actions.fix: Stop sending quotes from a gmail.com address
Stop chasing payment by phone for two weeks
priority_actions.outcome: Customers pay the invoice the same day

priority_actions.fix: Stop being the bad guy chasing overdue invoices

_roi_note: Section 03 Expected Outcomes uses sensible defaults; override per-client only where you need to. Common override: roi_value_amount to match the client's actual benefits subtotal.
roi_value_period: per month, plus A$30-45K of working capital released in the first year
roi_value_note: Most clients at your stage recover the A$880 engagement fee within the first 30 days through admin time saved alone — receivables compression is upside on top.

key_benefits.title: 12-15 hours back, monthly
key_benefits.body: Re-typing job sheets into MYOB on Sunday night disappears. Apprentices stop losing notes. Worth A$600-1200 to you at owner-operator rates.

key_benefits.title: Receivables tightened to 14 days
key_benefits.body: Chaser automates the polite-but-firm payment follow-ups. Industry average for trades drops 30 days when this is wired right. That's A$30-45K of working capital unlocked on a A$1M turnover.

key_benefits.title: A$184/month total software cost
key_benefits.body: Lean stack — each tool earns its keep. Detail in section 07. No spend until a tool's first job is queued up.

q_benefits_h2: What each move is worth, in hours and dollars.
q_benefits_lede: Conservative ranges. Owner-operator at A$60-120/hr, qualified tradesperson at A$50-80/hr, apprentice at A$25-40/hr.
benefits_basis_note: Hours estimated from your D-Manual self-report (12 hrs/wk re-typing) and AU industry benchmarks. Dollar values use Fair Work AU 2026 hourly rate bands. Working capital release assumes a A$1M annual turnover with trade-average 45-day to 14-day receivables shift.
recs_lede: Six tools, ordered by phase. Each one earns its keep against a specific phrase in your questionnaire.
cull: ServiceM8 holds customer history — a dedicated CRM is wasted spend at your volume.
Quotes go through ServiceM8 ‘Approve’ button. DocuSign is overkill until you're contracting on retainer.
Word-of-mouth is your engine. Mailchimp can come later when you have 200+ customers to email.
stack_glance_body: Each block hands off to the next. ServiceM8 captures the job, Xero handles the books, Stripe handles the card, Chaser does the chase, Calendly opens the booking door. Workspace is the spine.
phases_lede: Each phase ends with one capability fully live before the next is touched. No big-bang switch-overs.

phases.headline: Foundations — Workspace and Xero
tasks: Sign up for Google Workspace Business Starter at workspace.google.com
Configure hello@pacificcoastplumbing.com.au, set up email signatures with logo
Migrate from MYOB to Xero — import last 12 months of transactions
Set up the chart of accounts to match your job types

phases.headline: ServiceM8 live and apprentices on it
tasks: Sign up for ServiceM8 Growing plan at servicem8.com
Add 5 staff licences and load the team
Walk Friday morning toolbox meeting through the app — first jobs entered live
Wire ServiceM8 ↔ Xero native integration; first invoices syncing

phases.headline: Stripe and Chaser — receivables on autopilot
tasks: Connect Stripe to Xero — card payments accepted from invoices
Configure Chaser Starter — three-touch reminder cadence at 7, 14, 30 days
Set up branded Calendly link for quote-walk bookings
Standardise quote templates in ServiceM8 with your top 10 job types

phases.headline: Stability check — paper retired, books reconciled
tasks: Last paper job sheet entered; legacy MYOB read-only
60-day Xero reconciliation — books match bank, every transaction coded
First Chaser cycle complete — measure days-to-pay vs baseline
Apprentice retrospective: what's working, what isn't, what we missed

phases.headline: 90-day review and prep for Batch 01 digital employees
tasks: Pull the 90-day numbers: hours saved, dollars captured, days-to-pay
Scope Batch 01 of digital employees (see section 08) — pick the first one to build
Tighten the rough edges — quote templates, Chaser tone, ServiceM8 categories
Decide which Batch 01 agent goes first; book the discovery session

employees_h2: Three batches, scored on impact and readiness.
employees_lede: Nine agents, picked from a wider library and ordered into three phases. Batch 01 deploys on the Week 12 stack with no further foundation. Batch 02 needs the stack mature and a few months of history. Batch 03 is emerging upside — high ceiling, more setup.
employees_outro: Hours and dollars shown are conservative starting estimates — actual numbers depend on how each agent is used once live. We review every agent at the end of its batch before starting the next; if one isn't earning its keep, we stop and rethink rather than compound the spend.

batches.title: High impact, ready now.
batches.description: These agents are designed to deploy on the Week 12 stack. They don't need months of accumulated history or new infrastructure beyond what the rollout has put in place. Discovery, build, and supervised deployment still happen — but pay-back is measured in months, not years.

agents.name: Data-Sync Specialist
agents.description: Watches your ServiceM8 jobs and your Xero accounts; pushes line items from one into the other the moment a job is marked complete. No more Sunday-night re-typing. No more apprentices forgetting to file a docket.
agents.ties_to: Re-entering Friday's job sheets into MYOB on Sunday night

agents.name: Receivables Specialist
agents.replaces: Manual chase emails on overdue invoices
agents.description: Pairs with Chaser. Drafts the polite-but-firm follow-up, escalates the tone on schedule, posts the matched payment back to Xero when it lands. Average receivables window drops from 45 days to 14 in trades.

agents.name: Quote Builder
agents.description: Pre-fills ServiceM8 quotes from site-visit notes and your standard line items. You scan, adjust, send — typically within the hour the apprentice gets back to the depot.
agents.ties_to: We've started losing quote competitions to faster competitors

batches.title: High impact, foundation needed.
batches.description: These agents need the Week 12 stack to mature — a few months of customer history, a phone line connected, or a second tool wired in. High-impact when ready, but ship them too early and they don't have enough to work with.

agents.name: Lead Follow-up Specialist
agents.replaces: Quotes that go cold after no reply
agents.description: Knows which quotes haven't converted. Drafts the soft nudge at 7 days, the comparison-prompt at 14, the price-walk at 30. You stay in the conversation without remembering every name.
agents.ties_to: Quotes go out three days later

agents.name: Phone Reception Specialist
agents.replaces: Calls you miss because you're on a job or after hours
agents.hours: 8-12 hrs/mo of your time + revenue from missed calls
agents.readiness: Voice platform wired, FAQ knowledge base curated, ServiceM8 booking integration
agents.description: Takes inbound calls when your line is busy or after hours. Answers the standard questions from your curated FAQ, books emergency callouts straight into ServiceM8, and routes anything it can't handle to your mobile with the full call context already typed up. You stop missing calls. You stop being on call.
agents.ties_label: your preferred call time, which tells us your phone is always on

agents.name: Review-Request Specialist
agents.description: Fires a Google review request 24 hours after a job is marked paid. Personalises by job type. Industry-average for plumbing trades is 3% conversion — once you have 150 jobs/quarter, that's 4-5 new five-star reviews a month, compounding the next quarter's leads.

batches.title: Emerging upside.
batches.description: Higher ceiling, more setup. These agents either need the full stack mature plus six months of data, or they unlock strategic decisions rather than weekly time savings. Worth keeping on the horizon — not worth rushing.

agents.name: Profitability Analyst
agents.dollar: A$2,000-5,000/mo in margin from better pricing
agents.description: Reads every closed job in ServiceM8 against the Xero line items and tells you which jobs, which customers, which suburbs, which job types are actually paying your bills. Your gut probably knows; this gives you the receipts.
agents.ties_to: Without me being the bottleneck on every job

agents.name: Pricing Optimiser
agents.description: Tells you, by job type and customer profile, where you have pricing power and where you're leaving money on the table. The Quote Builder shapes the input; the Pricing Optimiser shapes the rate card.
agents.ties_to: Losing quote competitions to faster competitors

agents.name: Phone Agent Swarm
agents.replaces: A single phone agent that's hit its complexity ceiling
agents.hours: 16-24 hrs/mo of owner and team phone time
agents.dollar: A$1,000-3,000/mo + faster routing means more revenue captured
agents.readiness: Phone Reception Specialist proven, call-type segmentation captured, CRM mature enough to support routing
agents.description: Specialised siblings take different call types — emergency dispatch, scheduling, billing inquiries, quote follow-up. Each one knows its lane. They route to each other when a caller needs a different lane, and they only hand a call to a human when context demands it. Worth doing once the single Phone Reception Specialist has proven the pattern and you can see exactly where the call volume splits.
agents.ties_to: Grow to fifteen staff without me being the bottleneck on every job
